title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: On Monday your assistant helped a student plan a project. On Wednesday the same student opens a new chat and the assistant knows nothing about Monday. Your team built no storage for past chats. What explains this?

options.text: The context window was too small to hold two whole days of chat
The model keeps memories automatically but this one was switched off
Monday's context was never saved, so the new session starts empty
The model forgot Monday because it is trained only once a week

items.stem: In one run the model is called 3 times. The instructions plus tool list are 3,000 tokens and the question is 100 tokens. After call 1 the program adds 500 tokens (the tool request plus its result) to the context, and after call 2 it adds another 500. Each call is sent the whole context so far. Counting only input tokens, how many input tokens are read across all 3 calls?

Your manuals total about 300,000 tokens, which fits in the model's context window. Why would you still give the assistant a search tool that returns a few passages, rather than loading every manual into each request?

options.text: Because the API refuses any request that holds over 100,000 tokens
Because a model cannot read text that was not in its training data
Because search results are always more accurate than the full manual
Because every call would re-send and pay for it, and recall weakens

items.stem: In one or two words: what is the name for summarizing a conversation that is nearing the context limit and continuing in a fresh window that starts with that summary?
A student tells the assistant, "Always send my booking confirmations by email, never by text." Where should the assistant keep this so that it still applies on the student's next visit?

options.text: In a notes file for that student, which the next session reads
In the model itself, which learns it from the chat overnight
In the search index of manuals, beside the machine pages
In the context window, which stays open between the visits
